findings.reason: a node implementing exactly the three named writers ships a rule that leaves the meta stale on two landing writes, and the archive caller additionally needs a full state read before the opt-in can fire, which the plan does not say.
findings.text: §10 states "All three state writers pass the opt-in" and names the store write, `_replace_plan_text` and the `serve.py` POST handler, but `apply_archive_candidates` (`reckon/archive.py:132`, reached by `reckon archive --apply` via `run_archive_pass`) and `backfill_tags_from_preimage` (`reckon/tags.py:130`) also call `write_state` on a plan and write the result to disk; neither passes an opt-in, so a derived plan archived or retagged keeps its stale `plan-impl`, which is exactly the "stale for good, nothing repairs it" condition the section's Why sets out to end, and `archive.py` passes the partial dict `{"archived": "1"}`, so the opt-in's stated condition ("the state's impl is derived") cannot hold there even if it were passed — the opt-in's unstated precondition is a full `read_state`.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_plan_html.py:2281` (the `impl_source in {computed, declarations}` suppression in the lifecycle block), `_set_meta_block` (`_plan_html.py:2064`, which rewrites only the names it is given), `_store.py:1717` (the store write, with its parsed-state no-change guard at :1733-1748), `_store.py:2448` (the `write_state` call inside `_replace_plan_text`, whose identical-pair refusal is at :2390), `serve.py:3909` (the POST handler, `_content_equal` at :3911) and the cited measurement in `docs/plans/a-run-has-one-live-worker.html` (meta 0.67, declarations deriving 0.8579545 today) all resolve; the "141 plans under `docs/plans` carry a `plan-impl` meta" count reproduces exactly.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the five cases name three arms that fail at the dispatch base (a), (d), (e) and two keeps (b), (c), and the population is "the test files that import `reckon._plan_html`, `reckon._store` or `reckon.serve`" run at base and head, so the gate can fail and its negative controls are declared.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — "every log under the run directory starts with its revision and the literal command and ends in a bare `EXIT=` line", and the run directory is a durable path, not a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the test file and the opt-in are named by mechanism (`test_a_derived_impl_drops_the_authored_meta.py`), with no plan labels, section ids, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §10 claims all three state writers pass the opt-in, but two further production callers re-render a plan document with state and land the write, so the mechanism does not reach every path that writes a plan.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, a derived impl dropping the authored `plan-impl` meta; the three-writer list and the byte-identical default are scope for that one outcome, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10 declares no wire and needs none: §2, which creates the derived impl and the `impl-meta-stale` warning, and §7, which last rewrote `reckon/serve.py`, are both done, so no unlanded section holds this one.
